sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Florence restricts cars in the centre through its limited-traffic zone (ZTL), and a second, wider layer was added in 2025. The Scudo Verde environmental zone began operating in monitoring mode on 1 April 2025, covering about 38 km² with 77 gates, active 24 hours a day all year. The city says it adds no new bans and no toll, only applying environmental restrictions already in force, although tourist buses must buy an entry ticket [0]. The gates were technically activated on 1 June 2025 and fines were postponed to 1 July 2025 [1]. The launch had slipped from May 2024 after the Ministry of Infrastructure asked for further checks on the gates and signage [2]. The mobility assessor said Euro 4 vehicles would not be sanctioned and that no entry toll would be introduced through 2027 [3].

In the core sectors the ZTL runs Monday to Friday from 07:30 to 20:00 and on Saturdays until 16:00 [5]. Summer night restrictions apply from 23:00 to 03:00 on Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays, in force again from 2 April 2026 [4][5]. Electric vehicles may enter the ZTL after a free online authorisation [6]. For residents, the city planned to replace windscreen permits with digital ones from January 2025 [7]. Residents had to register their plates by 30 April 2025, with automated checks from 1 May, and additional resident zones cost €10 a month or €100 a year [8].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The main driver of change is the tram. Line T2 to the airport opened in 2019, with park-and-ride sites at Villa Costanza for the T1 and Guidoni for the T2 [10], and the tram carried over 39 million passengers in 2024, 11.8% more than in 2023 [11]. Building the new line 3.2.1 to Bagno a Ripoli has come with promises of replacement parking. In January 2025 it promised over 1,530 new spaces during the works, including 400 night spaces for residents in the Beccaria, Alberti and Parterre garages, and park-and-ride lots at Viale Europa (458 spaces) and Bagno a Ripoli (374; the figures differ between reports), which were said to open from April. That was a plan, not an opening [14]. Works on the Bagno a Ripoli site, with 358 spaces including 22 with EV charging, began in April 2024 [13], and night works on Viale Europa were scheduled for May 2026, with pre-service operation expected in early 2027 [12].

Garage pricing is also being used to steer demand. In October 2025, as the Piazza Beccaria works began, the Comune announced a 50% discount at the Piazza Alberti garage, from €2 to €1 an hour via the BMOVE app, from 22 October to December 2026, with free overnight parking for residents in Parterre, Beccaria and Alberti [15]. Telepass access is spreading, with 12 Florence garage structures counted by May 2026 [19], including the Santa Maria Novella station garage [20]. Florence recorded over 4 million tourist arrivals and 9.7 million overnight stays from January to October 2025 [24]. We found no sourced figures on a shift to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
All 13 garages in our Florence data, 5,718 spaces, are listed under one operator, Firenze Parcheggi. Few sit in the historic centre: only San Lorenzo (175 spaces, 0.5 km from the Duomo) lies within 500 m, and the 880-space Santa Maria Novella station garage is 0.9 km away. Seven garages with 2,728 spaces are 1 to 2 km out, and four with 1,935 spaces are further. The three garages within 500 m of the station hold 1,096 spaces. La Nazione reported the station garage at 570 spaces, against 880 in our data, and its 2023 revenue at €3.8 million [16].

Our prices run from €1.00 an hour at the outer Pieraccini Meyer, Careggi and Novoli garages to €4.00 at the station and San Lorenzo, with €2.00 at Parterre, Alberti, Fortezza, Porta al Prato and Beccaria. They differ from a May 2026 press list for some garages, for example Sant'Ambrogio, which it gave at €1.70 [18].

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 49% on weekdays and 45% at weekends. The busiest are Alberti (77% on weekdays, 66% at weekends, 313 spaces) and the station garage (71% and 70%), followed by Porta al Prato (60%) and Parterre (59%). The quietest is San Lorenzo (20% on weekdays, 175 spaces, €4.00), then Novoli (24%) and Pieraccini Meyer (28%). Price does not decide occupancy: the station and San Lorenzo both charge €4.00 and sit at opposite ends. Careggi CTO (43% on weekdays, 17% at weekends) and Novoli (24% and 6%) are far quieter at weekends, while the station garages stay level. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ, and we have no multi-year history for Florence.
